name: Padel (Chandarana Rhapta Road)
desc: Popular indoor/outdoor padel tennis courts at Rhapta Square, just down the road from the hotel. Courts are well-maintained and bookable by the hour. A great way to start the morning or burn off a long lunch.

name: ibis Styles (Saturday Night Live Band)
desc: Ibis Styles across from our hotel hosts a live band that draws a loyal local crowd. The energy is infectious, the drinks are cold and the setting is relaxed enough to stay late and crawl back to your room.

name: Drunken Lectures (Beer District)
desc: Every Monday night at Beer District, someone brilliant stands up and gives a talk while the audience drinks craft beer. Topics range from astrophysics to Kenyan hip-hop history. It’s free, informal, and genuinely one of the most interesting things happening in Nairobi on a weeknight. Walk to the venue and take a bodaboda back.

name: Siha Yoga Place
desc: A calm, well-run yoga studio tucked inside ABC Place on Waiyaki Way. They offer a range of classes from gentle Hatha to power Vinyasa, suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike. A welcome reset after a day of exploring the city.

name: Beit e Selam
desc: Food and drinks like their name are a reflection of Nairobi and influenced by the many culinary accents of the African continent. Great place to have a coffee, work or catch up with friends.

name: Furusato Japanese Restaurant
desc: One of Nairobi’s longest-running Japanese restaurants, known for its authenticity. The sushi is fresh, the teppanyaki is theatrical, and the menu runs deep enough to reward repeat visits. A favourite among the Japanese expat community, which tells you everything.

name: Unseen Nairobi
desc: An independent rooftop cinema screening art-house, African, and global indie films under the stars. The cocktail bar is excellent, the crowd is creative, and the programming is thoughtful. Check their schedule — screenings sell out quickly.

name: Monday Movie Nights at K1 Klub House
desc: Every Monday, K1 sets up an outdoor screen and projects a film for the crowd. It’s free. Be there by 6pm to get a good seat. They have complimentary blankets and offer free popcorn but you buy your food and drinks.

name: Habesha Ethiopian Restaurant
desc: Traditional Ethiopian dining in a peaceful garden setting. The injera is spongy and sour in all the right ways, the tibs are richly spiced, and eating with your hands from a shared platter makes the whole meal feel communal. Manager's recommendation: the mixed dish, Tej (honey wine), Ambo spring water, and don't leave without experiencing the coffee ceremony.

name: Nargis Restaurant Lavington
desc: A cozy neighbourhood spot in Lavington that’s earned a devoted following for its Masala Chips and Tandoori Chicken. The portions are generous, the spicing is bold, and the prices are reasonable. Perfect for a flavour-packed casual dinner.

name: Gochi Sake
desc: A refined sake bar and small-plates restaurant offering a curated selection of Japanese sakes alongside inventive bites. The atmosphere is intimate and the staff are knowledgeable enough to guide you through unfamiliar pairings. A standout for date nights.

name: A Little Bit of Everything (A.B.O.E)
desc: A trendy gastropub that lives up to its name with a menu spanning burgers, sushi, tacos, and more. The craft cocktails are creative and well-made, and the atmosphere is lively without being overwhelming. Great for groups who can’t agree on a cuisine.

name: Improv Nairobi
desc: A creative event space and community initiative putting on live comedy, spoken word, and variety shows. The performers are local, the energy is electric, and you’ll see a side of Nairobi’s arts scene that most visitors miss entirely. Check their IG for upcoming shows.

name: Birds of Paradise
desc: A unique, well curated studio offering aerial art, pole dance, aerial silks, hammock and hoop. The facilitators are warm and skilled, and the community around it is genuinely welcoming. Worth checking their schedule for upcoming workshops.

name: Hashmi Barbeque
desc: Fresh, hot, yummy Indian food.

name: Pickled
desc: Pickled has a vibe. When you walk in it's calm, it's green, it's very very nice. You end up staying longer than you planned without noticing. You will visit more than once. Highly recommend the hot honey halloumi, the Burrata Pesto, Bagel & Lox and Granola bowl.

name: The Good Grain
desc: A specialty coffee and pastry shop on the Slip Road off Waiyaki Way with carefully sourced beans and freshly baked goods. The space is small and focused, the baristas know their craft, and the pastries disappear fast — go early.

name: Geco Café (Kingara Road)
desc: An intimate venue on Kingara Road known for live jazz and acoustic band performances. The setting is warm and unpretentious, the musicianship is high, and the cocktails are good. Check ahead for the performance schedule — it fills up on popular nights.

name: Suave Restaurant & Lounge
desc: A contemporary dining spot that doubles as a cultural venue, hosting live music, art events and a hub for standup comedy. The food is solid, the interiors are designed with local artists' work, and the overall vibe feels like Nairobi's creative class at home.

name: Afrofit Gym
desc: A well-equipped gym at Delta Chambers in Westlands, just a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Great for keeping up your routine while travelling.

name: Afrofit Gym
desc: A well-equipped gym at Delta Chambers in Westlands, just a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Great for keeping up your routine while travelling.

name: Siha Yoga
desc: A serene yoga studio at ABC Place on Waiyaki Way offering daily classes across multiple disciplines. The instructors are experienced and attentive, and the studio is clean and well-equipped. Walk-ins welcome, but booking ahead guarantees your mat.

name: Birds of Paradise
desc: A holistic wellness space hosting regular sound healing, breathwork, and meditation sessions. The setting feels worlds away from Nairobi’s bustle, and the community is inclusive and grounding. Check their Instagram for the weekly schedule.

name: The Alchemist
desc: Nairobi’s most iconic open-air nightlife compound on Parklands Road. Multiple bars, food trucks, live DJs, and a wonderfully diverse crowd make it feel like a festival every weekend. Salsa Mondays are legendary, and the energy runs late into the night.

name: KODA Nairobi
desc: A newer, more intimate lounge and nightlife spot on Mkungu Close with a modern design sensibility. The cocktails are well-crafted, the music leans electronic and Afrobeat, and the crowd is stylish. A good pick for a more curated night out.

name: Nairobi Street Kitchen
desc: A multi-level outdoor destination on Mpaka Road combining street food vendors, cocktail bars, and a dance floor. Thursday is the legendary salsa and bachata night that packs the place. Come hungry, stay for the music.

name: Milan Lounge
desc: An upscale lounge in Mirage Tower on Westlands Road known for premium shisha, strong cocktails, and a well-dressed crowd. Live entertainment on select nights and a polished Sunday brunch. Open Wednesday through Sunday.

name: Cavalli @ The Manor
desc: A high-energy nightclub and lounge at 73 Westlands Road with a live band on Thursdays and top DJs spinning on weekends. The cocktails are surprisingly affordable, and the loyal crowd brings serious Friday and Saturday night energy.

name: K1 Klub House
desc: Nairobi’s beloved reggae institution, open 24 hours. Live bands play on Sundays, the drinks are reasonably priced, and the atmosphere is authentically local. Multiple bars spread across an open-air compound that feels like its own little neighbourhood.

name: Ciel Lounge
desc: A sophisticated rooftop lounge at Fortis Tower on Woodvale Grove with excellent cocktails and multiple seating areas. The atmosphere is refined but not stiff, the food is solid, and the service is attentive. Closed Mondays.

name: 11:11 Nightclub
desc: A high-energy nightclub on the 3rd floor of BroadWalk Mall with outstanding sound and lighting systems. Open Thursday through Sunday from 10 PM. No food service, so eat before you arrive — but once you’re in, the music carries the night.

name: La Terraza
desc: A vibrant spot at Promenade Mall on Rhapta Road, about a 15-minute walk from Kenya Continental. Great food, good drinks, and a lively terrace atmosphere that makes it worth the stroll.

name: Kosewe (Ranalo Foods)
desc: Right here in the Kenya Continental compound. Classic Kenyan cuisine at its finest — the fried tilapia, ugali, and sukuma wiki are exactly what locals eat at home, only better. A must-try for any guest who wants to taste real Nairobi.

name: Artcaffe (Rhapta Road)
desc: A reliable café-bistro just minutes from the hotel, serving everything from morning coffee and fresh pastries to full dinners and cocktails. The menu is broad, the quality is consistent, and the outdoor terrace is a pleasant spot to people-watch.

name: Pili Restaurant
desc: A contemporary fine-dining experience inside GTC Mall with generous portions and impeccable service. Their soups — particularly the pumpkin-potato and mushroom — are standouts. Beautiful views and booth seating make it worth booking ahead.

name: INTI — A Nikkei Experience
desc: High-end Japanese-Peruvian fusion at Delta Corner on Waiyaki Way. The ceviches are bright and precise, the maki rolls are inventive, and the cocktail programme draws from both traditions. One of the more distinctive dining experiences in Westlands.

name: Beit e Selam
desc: Food and drinks like their name are a reflection of Nairobi and influenced by the many culinary accents of the African continent. Great place to have a coffee, work or catch up with friends.

name: Anghiti Indian Restaurant
desc: Traditional Indian fine dining at Rehema House in Westlands. The tandoori dishes come out of the clay oven with real smoke and char, the curries are rich without being heavy, and the naan is made fresh to order. A reliable favourite for spice lovers.

name: 270 Rooftop
desc: A rooftop lounge and restaurant with sweeping panoramic views of the Nairobi skyline. The cocktails are well-mixed, the small plates are shareable, and the sunset hour is worth planning around. Best enjoyed in the evening when the city lights come on.

name: Sayari All Day Dining
desc: A 24-hour restaurant inside PrideInn Westlands serving Indian and continental dishes with generous portions. The late-night menu is a lifesaver after a long evening out, and the staff are consistently attentive. Perfect for group celebrations too.

name: About Thyme
desc: One of Nairobi’s most celebrated restaurants, set in a charming garden on Eldama Ravine Road. The teriyaki duck, moussaka, and ribs are perennial favourites, and the weekend brunch draws a loyal crowd. Closed Mondays.

name: Bao Box
desc: A playful, interactive café where you can dig into fresh steamed bao buns while challenging your table to a board game. The concept is fun, the food is surprisingly good, and it’s a refreshing change from the typical restaurant format.

name: Hashmi Barbeque
desc: A Nairobi institution at BroadWalk Mall, famous for its chooza chicken, spiced fries, and smoky Indian-style BBQ. The flavours are bold, the portions are huge, and the queues tell you everything about the quality. Come with an appetite.

name: Biscotti Café
desc: A warm neighbourhood café on Muthithi Road with excellent sambusas, margarita pizza, and a Lotus cheesecake that keeps people coming back. Perfect for a solo coffee date or a relaxed family lunch. The staff are genuinely friendly.

name: The Good Grain
desc: A specialty coffee and pastry shop on the Slip Road off Waiyaki Way with carefully sourced beans and freshly baked goods. The space is small and focused, the baristas know their craft, and the pastries disappear fast — go early.

name: Connect Coffee Roasters
desc: Nairobi’s specialty coffee temple on Chiromo Road. Single-origin pour-overs from Nyeri, Kilimanjaro blends, and baristas who genuinely care about extraction. Great wifi and power sockets make it a solid workspace too. Try the Kilimanjaro blend.

name: Café Kaya
desc: A rustic, homely café on the Slip Road off Waiyaki Way with board games, happy-hour cocktails (3 for KES 1,000), loaded cheesy fries, and samosas. The atmosphere is laid-back and genuinely cozy. Ideal for a quiet date or an afternoon with friends.

name: Black Olive
desc: A modern café on the 2nd floor of BroadWalk Mall with serious dark roast coffee and excellent avocado toast. It’s a reliable breakfast and lunch spot in the Parklands area, with a clean aesthetic and quick service.

name: Sip Spell Coffee Co.
desc: A charming outdoor café in Westlands that doubles as a fully vegetarian spot. The cinnamon buns are addictive, the Kenyan chai is brewed properly, and the shaded garden seating makes it perfect for a slow morning read or remote work session.

name: Midi Café & Patisserie
desc: French-inspired bakery and café inside the JW Marriott Hotel on Chiromo Lane. The pastries are handcrafted, the coffee is expertly brewed, and the setting has that polished hotel-lobby elegance. Perfect for a business meeting or an afternoon treat.

name: Artisan Blend Café
desc: A laid-back coffee lounge at Principal Place on School Lane with warm service and a welcoming atmosphere. Unusually, it stays open until 12:30 AM, making it one of Nairobi’s few late-night coffee options. Good food too.

name: Westlands Square
desc: A convenient shopping strip on Ring Road Parklands within walking distance of the hotel. It has a Quickmart supermarket, Java House, KFC, Optica, a spa, a salon, and a hospital all under one roof. Good for quick errands.

name: Sarit Centre
desc: One of Nairobi’s largest and most established malls on Lower Kabete Road. It has a cinema, bowling alley, rooftop garden, dozens of retail stores, restaurants, and a major supermarket. A one-stop destination that could easily fill an afternoon.

name: Westgate Shopping Mall
desc: A premium lifestyle mall on Mwanzi Road with international brands like Tommy Hilfiger, Hugo Boss, Mango, and Swarovski. The restaurants are excellent, the cinema is modern, and there’s a weekly Maasai market worth timing your visit for.

name: Geco Café (Kingara Road)
desc: An intimate venue on Kingara Road known for live jazz and acoustic band performances. The setting is warm and unpretentious, the musicianship is high, and the cocktails are good. Check ahead for the performance schedule — it fills up on popular nights.

name: Suave Restaurant & Lounge
desc: A contemporary dining spot that doubles as a cultural venue, hosting live music and art events. The food is solid, the interiors are designed with local artists’ work, and the overall vibe feels like Nairobi’s creative class at home.

name: Unseen Nairobi
desc: An independent rooftop cinema and cultural space showing African and global art films under the open sky. The cocktail programme is thoughtful, the audience is engaged, and the screenings are curated with real care. One of the city’s most original cultural spaces.

name: Afrika House (Holmes a Court Gallery)
desc: A private gallery showcasing contemporary East African fine art in a beautifully converted space. The exhibitions rotate regularly, the curation is strong, and visiting feels like stepping into the Nairobi art world’s living room. Call ahead to confirm hours.

name: Drunken Lectures
desc: Every Monday at Beer District, someone gives an unscripted talk on a fascinating topic while the audience drinks craft beer. The subjects are unpredictable, the speakers are passionate, and the discussions that follow are half the fun. Free entry.

name: Circle Art Gallery
desc: One of East Africa’s leading contemporary art galleries, located on Riara Road. The exhibitions spotlight emerging and established Kenyan and regional artists, and the space itself is worth the visit. Monthly openings are social occasions in their own right.

name: Monday Movie Nights at K1
desc: Every Monday, K1 sets up an outdoor screen and projects a film for the crowd. It’s free. Be there by 6pm to get a good seat. They have complimentary blankets and offer free popcorn but you buy your food and drinks.

name: Museum of Illusions
desc: An interactive optical illusion museum at Laxcon Court in Parklands that’s great for all ages. The exhibits are fun, the photo opportunities are endless, and you’ll need about an hour to see everything. Rated 4.7 stars for a reason.

name: National Museum of Kenya
desc: Kenya’s flagship museum on Museum Hill, covering human evolution, archaeology, natural history, and contemporary art. The Joy Adamson exhibit and Hall of Mammals are highlights. Allow 2–3 hours, and note that the Nairobi Snake Park is included in your ticket.

name: Nairobi Gallery
desc: A historic 1913 colonial building in the CBD housing the Murumbi African Heritage Collection — traditional textiles, masks, paintings, and artefacts from across the continent. Entry is very affordable via eCitizen, and the building itself is a landmark.

name: Karura Forest (Amani Garden)
desc: Over 1,000 hectares of indigenous forest just minutes north of Westlands with walking, running, and cycling trails, waterfalls, and a peaceful picnic garden. No single-use plastics are allowed inside. One of Nairobi’s finest escapes from the city’s pace.

name: Nairobi Arboretum
desc: A peaceful botanical garden off State House Road with over 300 tree species, resident monkeys, and quiet walking paths. Popular with joggers, families, and birdwatchers, it’s the kind of place where a morning walk can reset your entire day. Pet-friendly.

name: Nairobi National Park
desc: The only national park inside a capital city in the world. Lions, rhinos, giraffes, buffaloes, and zebras roam freely with the Nairobi skyline as a backdrop. Half-day game drives are available, and our front desk can arrange a morning safari departing at 6 AM.

name: Giraffe Centre
desc: Have you ever wanted to French kiss a giraffe? A conservation sanctuary on Duma Road in Langata where you can feed endangered Rothschild giraffes from a raised platform, eye to eye. The visit takes about 30 minutes and includes a nature trail and café. Card payment only — no cash.

name: Oloolua Nature Trail
desc: A forested hiking trail on Karen Road with waterfalls, caves, and mixed terrain that’s both scenic and adventurous. Bikes are available for hire, and entry is via eCitizen. Allow 2–3 hours for the full loop — it’s a wonderful half-day outdoor experience.

name: Sheldrick Elephant Orphanage
desc: A world-famous sanctuary for rescued elephant calves in Langata. The visiting window is strictly 11:00 AM – 12:00 PM, and advance booking is required. Watching the baby elephants mud-bathe and play is one of Nairobi’s most moving experiences. Don’t miss it.

name: Giraffe Centre
desc: Have you ever wanted to French kiss a giraffe? A conservation sanctuary dedicated to Rothschild giraffes with hand-feeding platforms that put you at eye level with these gentle giants. The attached nature trail is worth exploring, and the on-site café serves decent coffee. Family-friendly and unforgettable.

name: Afrika House (Holmes a Court Gallery)
desc: An exclusive fine art destination in Karen showcasing curated East African collections in a stunning private setting. The gallery rotates exhibitions regularly and offers a more intimate experience than the larger city galleries. Call ahead to arrange a visit.
